lines: I prefer danger in books. Books usually stay on the proper side of the shelf.
I made it home with shaking hands and all my important pieces.
The village door has never looked so welcoming.
I survived, though my notes from the fight are mostly crooked lines.
There were several moments when I expected a different ending.
I remember the noise better than the faces.
My knees started shaking only after we were safe.
I lost my bag, kept my life, and consider that a favorable exchange.
The first quiet breath afterward felt unreal.
I am going to sit near the lectern until my heartbeat behaves.
I learned exactly how fast I can run while carrying three books.
Home is a short word. It felt enormous when I reached it.
I can describe what happened once the order returns to my memory.
The danger passed. My body has not received that news yet.
I kept thinking of the door latch and whether anyone had opened it.
I am bruised, tired, and very glad to be complaining.
The account will be short because survival required no elegance.
I heard the bell behind me and followed the sound home.
I would like the next chapter of my life to contain fewer arrows.
We came back. For tonight, that is the only conclusion I need.
